raw_response:
I farm 5 mu of cotton, and at the start of the year I will mostly follow the way that has worked for me before, then adjust a little for cost and water. In our area, if I go too light on fertilizer and the cotton comes up weak, I cannot easily make that yield back later, so I would rather spend a bit more on base fertilizer and topdressing than gamble on a thin stand. I have well water, so I will not wait on the sky if the seedbed is dry or if flowering and boll setting run short of moisture. On 5 mu, the work is still manageable for two people, so I will keep it simple: improved seed, rotary tillage for fast land prep, enough phosphorus and potassium in the base, nitrogen split across the season, about 4 irrigations, and several pesticide sprays because cotton pests here can come in waves. I will aim for a steady field, not the highest possible input. If the stand is even and the water is timely, I will target around 330 kg seed cotton per mu.
